newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off on Dow, earnings, data fears.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off on Dow, earnings, data fears.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed lower in cautious trading Monday while traders awaiting economic data and first-quarter earnings reports.
"We basically followed the Dow (Jones)," a desk trader said. "Dealing was slow, they're apprehensive over first quarter reports, and this week also sees trade balance and inflation data."
The leading IPC share index was down 29.89 points, or 0.79 percent, at 3,758.54. Trading volume was lackluster at 59.02 million shares.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed down 43.34 points at 6,660.21.

Dealers said forthcoming inflation data were crucial to determining whether the central bank could cut interest rates. A Reuters survey of Mexico City financial houses predicted an average increase in consumer prices of 0.64 percent for the first hald of April.
Financial stock GFB, off four centavos (less than 1 cent) to 2.72 pesos (35 cents), was the most actively traded stock of the session.
"First quarter reports for financial stocks in general don't look like being so good," said one trader. "Look at Banacci, they hit it hard."
Banacci B shares fell 50 centavos (6 cents) to 16.98 pesos ($2.16) and ended near the head of the prominent decliners' list.

Telecomms firm Telmex L, off 28 centavos (4 cents) to 16.20 pesos ($2.06), also weighed heavily on the downside. Dealers said Telmex was paring sharp gains it made last week, and fell in tandem with its ADRs, which fell 3/4 to 41 in New York trading.
Telmex L and GFB B shares accounted for 42 percent of all shares traded during the session.
Retail stock Cifra, up 38 centavos (5 cents) to 11.68 pesos ($1.48), was the most heavily traded gainer, boosted by an improved earnings outlook.
"Cifra won't post a wonderful report, but at the least the slump looks like stopping," a trader said, referring to a slowdown in retail sales since the peso devaluation crisis of December 1994.
On the broad market, a total of 103 stocks were traded, of which sliders outnumbered gainers by 48 to 26.
